steps.tx: Dilated, tortuous surface veins of the leg from faulty valves are **varicose veins**. Failed valves let blood fall back down under gravity, stretching vein walls. Aching, itching and ankle swelling worsen through the day. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Varicose veins are dilated tortuous leg veins from faulty valves letting blood fall backwards.

vis.alt: Chronic venous disease and endovenous ablation.
vis.caption: Chronic venous disease and ablation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The junction where the long saphenous vein joins the deep femoral vein is the **saphenofemoral junction**. Valve failure here is the commonest source of reflux. Duplex scanning pinpoints exactly which junctions and segments leak. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: The saphenofemoral junction is the commonest reflux source and duplex scanning pinpoints leaks.

steps.tx: A bedside test locating the level of venous reflux is the **Trendelenburg test**. The leg is emptied, a tourniquet applied, and filling watched on standing. Controlled filling from below suggests deep or perforator problems instead. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: The Trendelenburg test locates venous reflux level by watching vein filling on standing.

steps.tx: Veins connecting surface and deep systems through the fascia are **perforators**. Their valves normally allow inward flow only. Incompetent perforators blast high pressure into skin veins and drive ulceration. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Incompetent perforators blast deep pressure into skin veins and drive ulceration.

steps.tx: Ultrasound mapping of reflux in standing patients is **venous duplex**. It has replaced bedside tests for treatment planning. The scan shows which veins to close and which to preserve. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Venous duplex maps reflux standing and has replaced bedside tests for treatment planning.

steps.tx: Sealing the faulty vein from inside with laser heat is **endovenous laser ablation**. Done under local anaesthetic, it avoids groin incisions and speeds recovery. Compression stockings follow for a short period. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Endovenous laser ablation seals faulty veins from inside under local anaesthetic with fast recovery.

steps.tx: Injecting irritant solution to close small veins is **sclerotherapy**. Foam preparations treat larger varicosities under ultrasound guidance. Skin staining and inflammation are the commonest unwanted effects. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Sclerotherapy injects irritant to close small veins, with skin staining as a common effect.

steps.tx: Open surgery tying the junction and stripping the vein is now reserved for selected anatomy, the classic **Trendelenburg operation**. Endovenous methods have largely replaced it. Recurrence follows any method if reflux sources are missed. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Open stripping is now selective since endovenous methods replaced it for most patients.

vis.alt: Stripped varicose long saphenous vein specimen.
vis.caption: Stripped saphenous vein specimen. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Graduated stockings remain the foundation for patients unfit for procedures, called **compression hosiery**. They counteract venous hypertension during standing. Correct fitting matters more than maximum tightness. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Compression hosiery counters venous hypertension and correct fitting matters more than tightness.
